title: Thread-safe keyed token-bucket rate limiter
spec:
The repository is empty. Create `ratelimit.py` (Python 3 stdlib only) with `class RateLimiter(capacity, rate, clock=time.monotonic, overrides=None)`: a token-bucket rate limiter keyed by client id.

**Model.** Every key has a bucket holding a (possibly fractional) number of tokens. A key's capacity is `overrides[key]` if given (or as last set by `set_capacity`), else `capacity`. `rate` is the refill rate in tokens per second, shared by all keys. A key that has never been used, or whose bucket has been discarded, has a full bucket. When a bucket is looked at, at time `t = clock()`, its level is `min(cap, tokens + (t - last) * rate)`, where `tokens` is the level recorded at time `last`. The clock never goes backwards. Keys can be any hashable objects; they need not be comparable with each other (e.g. `1`, `"a"` and an arbitrary object may appear in the same call).

**Validation.** `capacity`, `rate`, every override value, every requested token amount and every `set_capacity` capacity must be a positive int or float, otherwise `ValueError` is raised (before anything changes).

**API.** Every method is thread-safe, and every method except `__len__` reads `clock()` exactly once per call and uses that single reading throughout.
- `acquire(key, tokens=1) -> bool`: if the key's level is >= `tokens`, subtract `tokens` and return True; otherwise return False and change nothing. A request above the key's capacity therefore always fails.
- `try_acquire_many(requests) -> bool`: `requests` is any iterable of `(key, tokens)` pairs; amounts for a key that appears more than once are summed. All-or-nothing: if every key's level covers its total, debit all of them and return True; otherwise debit none and return False. It is atomic: no other thread may ever observe some of the debits without the others, or a temporary debit that is later rolled back. It must not deadlock, whatever order keys are given in by concurrent callers. An empty iterable returns True.
- `available(key) -> float`: the key's current level. It never creates or stores a bucket.
- `set_capacity(key, capacity)`: changes the key's capacity. If the key's bucket is full under its old capacity (at this call's clock reading), it is simply discarded, so the key starts again full at the new capacity. Otherwise its level is kept, clamped to the new capacity if that is lower.
- `len(limiter)`: the number of buckets currently stored.

**Bounded memory.** A full bucket is indistinguishable from a fresh one, so it must not be kept. A bucket is full at time t when its level equals its capacity, i.e. `tokens + (t - last) * rate >= cap`. After every call to `acquire` or `try_acquire_many` (successful, failed or empty) made at clock reading t, the limiter stores exactly the buckets of the keys that are not full at t; buckets of other keys that have refilled must have been discarded, and the limiter must keep no reference to their keys. This must be efficient: with tens of thousands of stored buckets, each call must cost far less than a scan of all of them (a test makes 50,000 `acquire` calls on distinct keys, with about 16,000 buckets alive at a time, and allows 10 seconds in total).

Tests use capacities, rates, token amounts and clock values that are exact in binary floating point (such as 0.25, 0.5, 2 ** -10), so the arithmetic above is exact. Inject the clock in your tests instead of sleeping, and add tests runnable with `python3 -m unittest -q`.
acceptance: refill, capacity overrides, set_capacity and fractional tokens behave exactly as specified
try_acquire_many is all-or-nothing, atomic to concurrent observers, sums duplicate keys and never deadlocks
no over-admission under heavy multi-threaded use
full buckets are discarded after every acquire/try_acquire_many, efficiently
